ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.claim: Sūrah Alam Nashraḥ completes the preceding sūrah: 93:6’s sheltering and other favours concerned the period before and just after prophethood, while this sūrah points to blessings after Islam spread in Arabia.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.anchor: It begins after Sūrah al-Ḍuḥā without any prior introduction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.claim: The prior sūrah predicts a bright future; this one points to predictions already beginning to materialize and assures the Prophet that hardship yields to success if faced courageously.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.anchor: by making a reference to some such predictions which by then had shown clear signs to materialize, an emphatic assurance is sounded to the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.claim: The discourse proceeds from inner expansion, through the recurring law of hardship with relief, to completion of the mission and disciplined use of its success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.anchor: Initially a reference is made to the gift of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r1.claim: The burden was the Prophet’s perplexity in seeking truth before prophethood and, later, the opposition of his people; his unanswered efforts and delayed revelation multiplied his worry.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r2.claim: The Prophet feared his preaching might be inadequate because people evaded it despite greater effort; Sūrah Ṭāhā similarly reassures that revelation was not meant to distress him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.claim: Lifting the burden is a metaphor for protection from sin and purification from defilement, expressed hyperbolically as if a burden had been removed from someone who had none.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.anchor: ووضعنا عنك وزرك: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس، عبر عن ذلك بالحط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r3.claim: Anqada describes a load making a camel's back creak under its weight; naqīḍ is a sound of cracking or coming apart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r3.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة، إذا سمعت له صريرا من شدة الحمل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r4.speaker: عباس بن مرداس وجميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r4.claim: Poets ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās and Jamīl use anqaḍa and naqīḍ as evidence for creaking under a burden and the sound of breaking ropes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r4.anchor: قال عباس بن مرداس: وأنقض ظهري ما تطويت منهم ... وكنت عليهم مشفقا متحننا

FARRA:v3p275#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p275#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
FARRA:v3p275#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī explains the burden that weighed on Muḥammad's back as sin.
FARRA:v3p275#2/r4.anchor: في تفسير الكلبي: الذي أثقل ظهرك، يعني: الوزر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r11.claim: Anqada means either making the back thin or defective under weight, or making a creaking sound like a loaded ship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r11.anchor: وأنقض معناه جعله نقضا، أي هزيلا معيبا من الثقل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497/r1.speaker: عباس بن مرداس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497/r1.claim: A poem by Abbas ibn Mirdas supplies an example for the sound or burden expressed by anqada.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497/r1.anchor: وأنقض ظهري ما تطوقت مضهم ... وكنت عليهم مشفقا متحننا

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r7.claim: Naqḍ and hadm are near-synonyms for destroying a structure by taking it apart; anqāḍ are loads nearly breaking what bears them.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r7.anchor: والنقض والهدم من النظائر، وهو إبطال البناء بالتفريق

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r17.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r17.claim: They explain anqaḍa as making something heavy; the expression compares the Prophet's back to a camel burdened and worn down by travel.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r17.anchor: قيل: أثقل، عن الحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r18.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r18.claim: He explains the phrase as breaking the back so that its sound is heard; this is a metaphor and simile.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r18.anchor: وقيل: كسر ظهرك حتى سمع نقيضه؛ أي: صوته، عن الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says the burden made the Prophet's back heavy, like a camel strained by a heavy load.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r11.anchor: قاله ابن زيد كما ينقض البعير من الحمل الثقيل حتى يصير نقضا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r12.claim: Mawardi gives three possible burdens: sins later forgiven, the message to deliver, or blessings for which to give thanks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r12.anchor: أحدها : أثقل ظهره بالذنوب حتى غفرها . الثاني : أثقل ظهره بالرسالة حتى بلغها

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Sharḥ Makkan and place it just after Sūrah 93; Ibn ʿAbbās calls it Madinan, while some assign only vv. 5–6 to Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.anchor: considered by most commentators to be a Makkan sūrah, most likely revealed immediately after the preceding one. Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that it is Madinan

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.claim: Some say Sūrahs 93 and 94 were originally one, since Companions recited them together in one prayer cycle without a basmalah separating them.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.anchor: the Companions of the Prophet would recite them together in a single prayer cycle

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.claim: Ash-Sharh was revealed almost immediately after Ad-Duha and appears to continue it directly.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.anchor: revealed almost immediately af ter the preceding one, appears to be a direct continuation of the latter

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.speaker: Ta'us ibn Kaysan and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.claim: They regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah and recited them in prayer without a second basmala; Asad cites Razi.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.anchor: Ta'us ibn Kaysan, or the Caliph Umar i bn Abd al-Aziz (known as "the Second Umar") - regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.claim: The surah addresses the Prophet first and, through him, every true follower of the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.anchor: addressed in the first instance to the Prophet and, through him, to every true follower of the Qur'an

BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r3.claim: The burden made the back creak; dictionaries explain أنقض as breaking noisily or weighing someone until the load's saddle parts groan under its weight.
BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r3.anchor: أي حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الانتقاض والانفكاك كما يسمع من الرحل

QASHANI:94:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:94:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:94:1/r3.claim: The prophetic burden is carrying revelation and duties: in witnessing, the Prophet saw only God and could not distinguish acts or command and forbid; returning from sainthood to prophethood, the heart’s veil nearly broke his back. Empowerment in abiding lets him see unity in multiplicity without losing witness during the call, removing the burden and raising his mention.
QASHANI:94:1/r3.anchor: ثقل ذلك عليه وكاد أن يقصم ظهره لاحتجابه عن الشهود الذاتي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the burden is Muhammad's sin, which weighed heavily on him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ووضعنا عنك وزرك قال : ذنبك الذي انقض ظهرك قال : اثقل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.claim: Mujahid notes that Abdullah's reading has 'we relieved you of your burden.'
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : في قراءة عبد الله ' وحللنا عنك وقرك '

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.claim: The burden was removed in part by guidance to truth, which ended the Prophet's distress over his people, and by provision for a livelihood that could distract him from reflection on reform.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.anchor: وأما وضع الوزر عنه فحاصل بأمرين : بهدايته إلى الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r1.claim: The burden weighed on the Prophet until his back seemed to make a sound; the verse is a simile for that weight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r1.anchor: أثقله حتى سمع نقيضة أي صوته وهذا مثل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r2.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r2.claim: Some interpret the burden as the heavy responsibilities of prophethood, which God made easier for the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p163/r2.anchor: ذهب قوم إلى أن المراد بهذا تخفيف أعباء النبوة التي يثقل القيام بها الظهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r2.claim: Al-inqad means a sound or creaking; several early authorities explain that the burden weighed heavily on Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r2.anchor: الإنقاض: الصوت. وقال غير واحد من السلف في قوله: {الذي أنقض ظهرك} أي: أثقلك حمله.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#4/r1.claim: “It weighed down your back” means the burden was so heavy its creaking sound could be heard; this is a metaphor.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#4/r1.anchor: {أنقض ظهرك} أثقله حتى سمع نقيضه، أي صوته (2) وهذا مثل.

MUJAHID:v2p767#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p767#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p767#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the burden made the Prophet’s back heavy.
MUJAHID:v2p767#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ الذي أنقض ظهرك ﴾ أثقل ظهرك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#3/r1.claim: The burden weighed on the Prophet until his back made a cracking sound like a joint being strained.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ الذي أنقض ظهرك ﴾ أثقله حتى سمع نقيضه

NAHHAS:v5p251/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p251/r11.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v5p251/r11.claim: Exegetes say the burden weighed the Prophet down.

NAHHAS:v5p251/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p251/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p251/r12.claim: Though forgiven, a burden may feel heavy because prophets and righteous people grieve and weep when recalling their sins.
NAHHAS:v5p251/r12.anchor: أن سبيل الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم والصالحين إذا ذكروا ذنوبهم أن يشتد غمهم وبكاؤهم

NAHHAS:v5p251/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p251/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p251/r13.claim: Another answer is that the righteous fear some obligation of complete repentance remains outstanding.
NAHHAS:v5p251/r13.anchor: وهو أنهم يخافون أن يكونوا قد بقي عليهم شيء بلزمهم من تمام التوبة

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r5.claim: The burden made the Prophet's back so heavy that its creaking could be heard; linguists use the same expression for a load that makes a camel's back creak.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r5.anchor: أي أثقله حتى سمع نقيضه أي صوته. وأهل اللغة يقولون:

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r6.speaker: جميل
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r6.claim: Jamil's line about ropes creaking until their supports nearly break provides poetic evidence for naqidh as a creaking sound under strain.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.claim: Bawani al-zawr means the foundations of the chest, and burden means a heavy load; al-Muhasibi says it would have remained weighty had God not pardoned it.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.anchor: «بواني زوره»: أي أصول صدره. فالوزر: الحمل الثقيل. قال المحاسبي:

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.claim: Al-Muhasibi explains why forgiven prophetic sins are described as heavy: prophets are deeply concerned, regretful, and sorrowful about them.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.anchor: قال: وإنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء بهذا الثقل، مع كونها مغفورة، لشدة اهتمامهم بها،

QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet's back almost to breaking; God removed it by opening his heart, making the task lighter and easier.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.anchor: عبئك الذي أثقل ظهرك حتى كاد يحطمه من ثقله

QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.claim: God eased the burden by enabling the mission, opening hearts to it, and sending revelation that disclosed truth and helped convey it gently to people.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.anchor: وبتوفيقك وتيسيرك للدعوة ومداخل القلوب . وبالوحي الذي يكشف لك عن الحقيقة

QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet's back almost to breaking; God removed it by opening his heart, making the task lighter and easier.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.anchor: عبئك الذي أثقل ظهرك حتى كاد يحطمه من ثقله

QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.claim: God eased the burden by enabling the mission, opening hearts to it, and sending revelation that disclosed truth and helped convey it gently to people.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.anchor: وبتوفيقك وتيسيرك للدعوة ومداخل القلوب . وبالوحي الذي يكشف لك عن الحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.claim: The judge criticizes a report in which the Prophet asks why others received special favors: prophets only ask with permission, and God's reply sounds reproachful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.anchor: فهل يصح هذا الحديث قلنا : طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر فقال : إن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يسألون مثل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.claim: The chest is named because Satan's whispering occurs there; expansion removes whispering and replaces it with good impulses.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.anchor: لأن محل الوسوسة هو الصدر على ما قال : { يوسوس فى صدور الناس }

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.claim: The heart is the seat of reason and knowledge, guarded by the chest; if Satan enters the chest he brings worry, grief, and greed, constricting the heart and spoiling worship, while early resistance restores ease.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي الترمذي : القلب محل العقل والمعرفة ، وهو الذي يقصده الشيطان

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.claim: The phrase 'for you' may indicate reciprocity: the Prophet performs all worship for God, and God performs His acts for the Prophet; alternatively, the mission's benefit returns to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.anchor: وثانيها : أن فيها تنبيها على أن منافع الرسالة عائدة إليه عليه السلام ، كأنه تعالى قال : إنما شرحنا صدرك لأجلك لا لأجلي

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.claim: Using 'We' either magnifies the gift beyond comprehension or includes God's angels, whose presence strengthened the Prophet and made his opponents afraid.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.anchor: إن حملناه على نون التعظيم ، فالمعنى أن عظمة المنعم تدل على عظمة النعمة

RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r3.speaker: علماء اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r3.claim: Linguists explain anqaḍ as the faint sound a heavily loaded back makes; the phrase metaphorically evokes burdens weighing on the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r3.anchor: الأصل فيه أن الظهر إذا أثقل الحمل سمع له نقيض أي صوت خفي

SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r1.claim: Anqaḍa ẓahraka compares the burden to a heavy load making the back creak and crack; Arabic speakers use the verb for a camel's back under strain.
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r1.anchor: أي: حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الانتقاض والانفكاك لثقله

SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r2.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r2.claim: Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās uses anqaḍa ẓahrī for a heavy burden he endured on behalf of his people.
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r2.anchor:
وأنقض ظهري ما تطويت منهم
وكنت عليهم مشفقا متحننا

SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r3.speaker: جميل
SAMIN-DURR:94:3/r3.claim: Jamīl's line describes ropes breaking with a creaking sound, supporting the sense of naqīḍ.

STUDYQURAN:94:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:3/r1.speaker: al-Bayḍāwī
STUDYQURAN:94:3/r1.claim: Anqaḍa describes a load pressing so heavily that the back makes a sound.

STUDYQURAN:94:3/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:3/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:94:3/r2.claim: Some read the burden as the weight of prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:94:3/r2.anchor: Some say this verse refers to God’s lightening the burden of prophethood

TAB:94:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r3.speaker: author
TAB:94:1/r3.claim: Putting down the burden means forgiving past sins and removing the weight of the days of ignorance before Islam.
TAB:94:1/r3.anchor: وغفرنا لك ما سلف من ذنوبك ،   وحططنا عنك ثقل أيام الجاهلية التي كنت فيها

TAB:94:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:94:1/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the burden as Muhammad's sin and the phrase about his back as making it heavy.
TAB:94:1/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ،   عن مجاهد في قول الله :  وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  ذنبك

TAB:94:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:1/r6.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had sins that weighed him down, and God forgave them.
TAB:94:1/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمَ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ

TAB:94:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r9.speaker: author
TAB:94:1/r9.claim: Anqada means that a load made the back heavy and weak; the term evokes a camel worn down by a burdensome journey.
TAB:94:1/r9.anchor: الذي أثقل ظهرك فأوهنه ،   وهو من قولهم للبعير إذا كان رجيع سفر ،   قد أوهنه السفر

TAB:94:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:94:3/r1.claim: Anqada means to make the back heavy; Ibn Zayd likens it to a camel whose heavy load makes it waste away after being fat.
TAB:94:3/r1.anchor: وفي قوله :  الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ قال :  أثقله وجهده ،   كما يُنْقِضُ البعيرَ حِمْله الثقيل

TAB:94:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:3/r2.claim: Qatada says Muhammad had sins that weighed him down and that God forgave them.
TAB:94:3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمَ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ

TAB:94:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:3/r3.claim: A second transmission from Qatada repeats that the Prophet's burdensome sins were forgiven by God.
TAB:94:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ قال :  كانت للنبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

TAB:94:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:94:3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God expanded Muhammad's chest and forgave his sin from before prophethood.
TAB:94:3/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  ألَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  شرح له صدرَه

TAB:94:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:94:3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the burden exhausted the back as a heavy load wears down a camel, then God lightened it.
TAB:94:3/r6.anchor: قال :  أثقله وجهده ،   كما يُنْقِضُ البعيرَ حِمْله الثقيل ،   حتى يصير نِقْضا بعد أن كان سمينا

TAB:94:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r7.speaker: author
TAB:94:3/r7.claim: The removed burden is described as Muhammad's sin that weighed down his back; God lifted it and made the load lighter.
TAB:94:3/r7.anchor: قال :  ذنبك الذي أنقض ظهرك :  أثقل ظهرَك ،   ووضعناه عنك ،   وخفّفنا عنك ما أثقل ظهرَك

TABRISI:94:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:94:1/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:94:1/r3.claim: Anqad are loads that make what bears them creak; naqḍ and demolition are equivalent, and a camel is described as weighed down by travel.
TABRISI:94:1/r3.anchor: والأنقاض الأثقال التي كان ينتقض بها ما حمل عليه والنقض والهدم واحد

TABRISI:94:2-3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:94:2-3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:94:2-3/r4.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet so heavily that, had it been a physical load, one would hear his back creak.
TABRISI:94:2-3/r4.anchor: أي أثقله حتى سمع له نقيض أي صوت عن الزجاج

ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r1.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r1.claim: Tabari, citing Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd, identifies the burden as past sins that have now been forgiven.
ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r1.anchor: Tabari, on the authority of Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd

ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r2.claim: For Muhammad this apparently refers to mistakes before prophethood and echoes 93:7, where he was found lost and guided.
ASAD-NOTES:94:1#n2/r2.anchor: this relates apparently to mistakes committed before his call to prophethood

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125/r1.claim: The interpreters gloss “weighed down your back” as “made your back heavy,” citing Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Muqātil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125/r1.anchor: {الذي أنقض ظهرك} قال المفسرون: أثقل ظهرك. وهو قول ابن عباس (¬1)، ومجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r1.claim: The word evokes the faint sound made by an overloaded back; God forgave burdens that would have made such a sound if they were literal loads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r1.anchor: قال علماء اللغة: الأصل فيه أن الظهر إذا أثقله الحمل سمع له نقيض أي: صوت خفي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r2.claim: Anqaḍa means that the burden became so heavy it produced a faint sound; the image is a metaphor for a weighty load.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: {أنقض ظهرك} هو: أثقله حتى سمع له نقيض، أي صوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r3.claim: A line about grief says it makes the ribs creak; the cited form anqaḍa also describes a cupping glass or a nestling audibly chirping.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r3.anchor: وحزن تنقض الأضلاع منه ..... مقيم في الجوانح لن يزولا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r4.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's phrase “anqāḍ al-farārīj” is another lexical example of the creaking or chirping sound.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r4.anchor: يقال (¬4): أنقض إنقاضا، ومنه قول ذي الرمة: أنقاض الفراريج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had sins weighing on him, and God forgave them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r5.anchor: قال قتادة في هذه الآية: كانت للنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- ذنوب قد أثقلته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.claim: One interpretation says the sins occurred before prophethood, in the pre-Islamic period.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.anchor: هذا الذي ذكرنا في الآيتين على قول من يقول: كانت له ذنوب سلفت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.claim: Others identify the burden as minor sins, mistakes, or lapses; although forgiven, they distressed the Prophet because he regretted and grieved over them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن المراد بهذا: الصغائر، والخطأ، والسهو، وإنما وصف ذلك بإنقاض الظهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that God eased the burdens of prophethood—its duties, preservation, and rights—by making them manageable; al-Kisāʾī and Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk are associated with this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكسائي (¬1)، وجويبر عن الضحاك

WAHIDI-QT:94:3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:94:3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:94:3/r1.claim: The burden had weighed heavily on Muhammad's back.

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r2.claim: Inqada evokes ruin, a weakened camel, and crackling or squeaking under strain; the back-crushing image portrays earlier hardships as a heavy load.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r2.anchor: Burada murad Peygamber’e mukaddemâ tahammülü ağır gelmiş olan zorlukların böyle bir bâr-ı girân hey’etinde temsîlen tasvîridir

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r3.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r3.claim: Some lexicographers emphasize the camel weakened by travel, while many understand the sound of bones creaking and cracking under a heavy load.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r3.anchor: Bazıları, nıkz deve gibi zayıflanmak mânasından, çokları da nakīz çıkarmaktan kemikleri gıcırdatmak, çatırdatmak

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r4.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir says the burden weighed on the back and weakened it, using the Arab term for a camel exhausted by a journey.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r4.anchor: İbn Cerîr demiştir ki: “أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ zahrına ağır bastı da ona

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r5.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r5.claim: Razi and other scholars cite lexicographers who explain nakiz as the faint sound made when a load presses heavily on a back, ribs, or camel.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r5.anchor: Râzî ve sâirleri de demişlerdir ki: “Lügat ulemâsı şöyle dediler

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r6.claim: Elmalılı rejects forcing inqada into a transitive sense: the sound belongs to the heavy burden on the Prophet's back and conveys how painfully he felt it.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r6.anchor: Lâkin burada أَنقَضَ’ya böyle müte‘addî mânası verilmek için çalışılmasına benim gönlüm pek razı olmuyor

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r7.claim: He reads zahr as locative, with an understood fi, meaning that the burden on the Prophet's back creaked and hurt him; this is more natural than metonymically assigning the sound to the back.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r7.anchor: Bu ses Resûlullah’ın sırtına değil, sırtındaki o ağır yüke, vizre ait olmalı. Murad da Resûlullah’ın arkasındaki o ağır yükün gıcırtısından

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r8.speaker: Bir kısım müfessirîn
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r8.claim: Some exegetes read vizr as heavy sin, citing 6:31, and interpret removing it as forgiveness like 48:2.

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.claim: Elmalılı rejects the sin reading as unlikely: vizr's weight and the emphatic back-crushing description do not suit minor lapses that can be attributed to prophets.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.anchor: Onun için bunun günah mânasına değil ağır yük, hıml-i sakīl, bâr-ı girân mânasıyla Peygamber’i nübüvvetten evvel

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.claim: He prefers burdensome difficulties before or at the beginning of prophethood, the majority's choice; an alternative says the Prophet's exceptional sensitivity made even a small lapse weigh heavily.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.anchor: olabilirse de hilâf-ı zâhir olmaktan kurtulmaz

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.claim: One proposed burden was the bewilderment of seeing pre-Islamic society's idolatry and ignorance, while recognizing God's blessings yet not knowing how to serve Him; revelation removed that distress.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.anchor: Nübüvvet gelince bu hayret zâil olmuş, onun muktezâsı olan vizir üzerinden atılmıştır

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.claim: Burden and sin converge as spiritual pain, but differ in outcome: hardship's pain can end in reward and pleasure, whereas sin's pleasure leads to later pain.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.anchor: Gönülde duyulan gam ve eleme “vizr” tâbir edilmesi bu itibar iledir. Ancak yük elemi zâil olarak sonu bir ecr ü hazza müntehî olmak

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.claim: A generous person feels ashamed to enjoy gifts without serving their giver; when service is offered, even heavy work becomes welcome and light, as happened when prophethood gave the Prophet a path of service.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.anchor: Kerîm, âlîcenab kimse ise gördüğü in‘âma karşı hizmet edememiş veya o nimeti yerine sarf eyleyememiş olmaktan sıkılır

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.claim: A second proposed burden was the grave responsibility and fear of properly receiving and carrying out the prophetic mission, and of failing before God and people.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.anchor: O da risâlet vazifesinin hakkıyla telakkī ve îfâsındaki azîm meşakkat ve mes’ûliyet endişesi

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.claim: As knowledge and recognition increase, fear of God grows, in keeping with 35:28.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.anchor: ilim ziyadeleşip marifet arttıkça haşyetullah da artıyor

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.claim: At his first meeting with Gabriel, the Prophet trembled under the awe of the powerful angel described in 53:5–6.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.anchor: Evvelâ Cibrîl’e ilk mülâkātında bütün cühd ü tâkatini saran

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.claim: After gradually adapting to revelation, he faced unbelievers' abuse and hostility before receiving the promise of protection in 5:67 or the glad tidings in 93:4–5.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.anchor: kâfirlerin o zamana kadar görülmeyen ezâ ve cefâ ve türlü dedikodularla husûmet ve adâvetlerini görmeye başlamıştı

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.claim: The temporary cessation of revelation, loneliness, and mockery also grieved him and added to his worldly and otherworldly anxieties.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.anchor: Bir müddet için dinlendirilmek üzere vahyin fetret ve inkıtâ‘ından dolayı duyduğu yalnızlık ve işittiği şemâtetten dolayı

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.claim: With continued revelation and al-Duha, God removed some burdens and lightened others through habituation and greater insight, giving the Prophet spiritual strength and making the world seem negligible.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak, vahyin tevâlîsi ve Ve’d-duhâ’nın inzâliyle bunların bir kısmını büsbütün üzerinden atmış, bir kısmını da alıştırmak

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.claim: Through the Qur'an's blessing, God began to raise the Prophet's name, honor, and standing in this world and the Hereafter.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.anchor: Kur’ân’ın feyziyle dünya ve âhiret nâm u şânını, zikir ve haysiyetini yükseltmeye başlamış idi

CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.claim: Psalmic imagery may underlie the phrase, especially Psalm 4:2’s image of God making room in distress; the opening also directly uses the divine ‘we’ as in 97:1 and 108:1.
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Wie auch in V. 2 und 4 könnte dabei eine psalmische Bildsprache im Hintergrund stehen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.claim: The burden removed may be the Prophet's anguish at his society's faith and morals, quieted or eased when revelation gave him hope and relief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.anchor: arasında yaşadığı topluluğun inanç ve ahlâk yönünden içine düştüğü durumdan dolayı duyduğu ıstırabın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.claim: Alternatively, God removed the burden by granting support in establishing monotheism and virtues such as justice, honesty, mercy, and cooperation in good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.anchor: Tevhid inancını ve insan ilişkilerinde adalet, dürüstlük, merhamet, iyilikte yardımlaşma gibi erdemleri hâkim kılma mücadelesinde

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p380/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p380/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p380/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had sins weighing heavily on him, which God forgave.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p380/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أنقض ظهرك ﴾ قال كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r1.claim: أنقض means to make a creaking or cracking sound as joints loosen; it also applies to joints, not only loads or people, and the line of Abbas ibn Mirdas depicts a burden making his back groan.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r1.anchor: الذي انقض ظهرك أي حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الأنتقاض والأنفكاك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r2.claim: Attributing the creaking to the load is a figurative attribution to its causing agent; the burden can mean pre-mission acts the Prophet found painful to recall, with its removal meaning forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r2.anchor: وإسناد الإنقاض للحمل إسناد للسبب الحامل مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r3.claim: Other proposed burdens are the Prophet's lack of revealed knowledge of religious law, uncertainty about the message or its reception, and the difficulty of receiving revelation at first; removal means teaching or easing these matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r3.anchor: أو غفلته عن الشرائع ونحوها مما لا يدرك إلا بالوحي مع تطلبه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r4.claim: Other explanations are grief at his people's misguidance while unable to guide them, their abuse of him, or anxiety over Abu Talib's death and Khadija's death if the surah followed theirs; relief comes through converts such as Hamza and Umar or strengthened endurance.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r4.anchor: أو ما كان يرى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من ضلال قومه مع العجز عن إرشادهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r5.claim: The removal is also interpreted as lifting the Prophet to heaven, where he met every angel and attained the vision of his beloved Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r5.anchor: وعلى السابع إزالة ذلك برفعه إلى السماء حتى لقيه كل ملك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r6.claim: Whatever the intended burden, the expression is a representative metaphor, and the verse does not prove the Prophet was previously without protection from sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r6.anchor: وأيا ما كان ففي الكلام استعارة تمثيلية والوضع ترشيح لها وليس فيه دليل لنا في العصمة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the burden as sins and the removal as the Prophet's protection from sin and purification, phrased as a rhetorical exaggeration.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r7.anchor: واختار أبو حيان كون وضع الوزر كناية عن عصمته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r8.claim: A further view makes the burden the sins of Muhammad's community, attributed to him because of his concern for them; its removal means preventing their immediate punishment while he is among them or they seek forgiveness, as in 8:33. Al-Alusi calls this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r8.anchor: والتمثيل عليه بحاله على ما قيل المراد وزر أمتك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r9.claim: Anas reads حططنا or حللنا instead of وضعنا, while Ibn Masud reads عنك وقرك.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ أنس وحططنا وحللنا مكان وضعنا وقرأ ابن مسعود عنك وقرك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r6.claim: The burden made the Prophet's back heavy and weak until it made a sound, called naqīḍ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r6.anchor: أثقل ظهرك فأوهنه حتى سمع له نقيض، أي صوت

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r5.claim: That burden may be pre-mission lapses, ignorance of rulings, bewilderment, the difficulty of receiving revelation, grief at his people's error, or their persistence and abuse when he called them to faith.
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r5.anchor: من ثقل الحمل وهو ما ثقل عليه من فرطاته قبل البعثة، أو جهله بالحكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.claim: A report likens reciting this sura to visiting the Prophet while distressed and relieving him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة ألم نشرح فكأنما جاءني وأنا مغتم ففرج عني

BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.claim: In both literal and figurative Quranic uses, waḍʿ evokes relief from a heavy load: war's burdens, weapons, shackles, and the Prophet's burden.
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.anchor: فشهد هذا التتبع الاستقرائي، على أن الوضع ملحوظ فيه دائماً، التخفف من ثقل مرهق وحمل باهظ

BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.claim: Wizr first means a mountain and by extension a refuge; wazīr shares the load, and the term then denotes physical weight or moral sin.
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.anchor: وأصل الوزر: الجبل، وسمى الملجأ وزراً

BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.claim: The paired image of removing the burden and the burden that made the back give way emphasizes how oppressive its weight had been.
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.anchor: والوضع للوزر في آية الشرح، يؤكد ثقل العبء، كما تؤكده الآية بعدها

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan quotes linguists who describe a load making a camel's back creak under its weight, like a pot making a noise.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r1.anchor: أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة إذا سمعت له صريراً من شدة الحمل

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the sound a creaking or splitting caused by the weight; Abduh gives a similar explanation.

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r3.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r3.claim: Al-Raghib rejects making inqāḍ itself the sound: it is the underlying giving way that produces the noise.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r3.anchor: وحقيقة الانتقاض ليس الصوت، إنما هو الذي يحدث منه الصوت

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r4.claim: The author favors a sense of crushing weight that loosens or splits the back, preserving the Quran's broader use of naqḍ for undoing things.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r4.anchor: ونؤثر أن يكون الإنقاض من الإثقال الذي يحل الظهر

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.claim: Al-Raghib reads the burden as the customs of pre-Islamic ignorance from which Muhammad was specially exempted.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.anchor: هو ما كنت فيه من إصر الجاهلية، وأعفيت منه بما خصصت به

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan interprets the burden figuratively as protection from sins and purification from defilement.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.anchor: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the burden as past sins forgiven and the weight of the Prophet's earlier days lifted.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.anchor: وغفرنا لك ما سلف من ذنوبك، وحططنا عنك ثقل أيام الجاهلية

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.speaker: قتادة
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had sins that weighed on him, which God forgave.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.anchor: كانت للنبي ذنوب قد أثقلته فغفرها تعالى له

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the burden as shirk; the author corrects this to the shirk of Muhammad's people.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.anchor: والأولى عندنا أن يقال: الشرك الذي كان فيه قومه.

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.claim: Other interpretations include pre-prophetic minor sins, ignorance of revealed laws, intense concern to bring stubborn people to Islam, the burdens of the mission, or pre-revelation bewilderment.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.anchor: وقيل: ما أثقل ظهره لما صدر عنه من بعض الصغائر قبل النبوة

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.claim: Abduh reads the image as the crushing psychological burden of concern for his people and uncertainty before revelation, heavier than any physical load.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.anchor: ما كان يحمله عليه السلام من ثقل الاهتمام بشأن قومه، وضيق المذاهب بين يديه

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.claim: The author agrees with Abduh: the burden is the pre-revelation confusion and failure to find the straight path described in 93:7.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.anchor: فالوزر في الآية هو من: ضلال الحيرة وعدم الاهتداء إلى سواء السبيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.claim: The burden was the strain of warning people by condemning their religion, ancestors, and judgment, which provoked their pride and threats of violence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.anchor: ما دهمه عندما أمر بإنذار قومه ومفاجأتهم بما يكرهون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar b. al-Zubayr says al-Sharḥ continues al-Ḍuḥā's theme: both chapters enumerate God's favors to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.anchor: معنى هذه السورة من معنى السورة قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.claim: The chapters are separate because a benefactor first recounts favors that could seem earned, then original gifts granted before the recipient existed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.anchor: من المعهود في البشر فيمن عدد على ولده أو عبده نعما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.claim: The analogy is a parent first listing visible acts for a child, then the prior choice of the mother and provision made before the child's existence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.anchor: أن يذكر له أولا ما شاهد الحصور عليه منها بسببه

DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.claim: He says the Prophet's breast was filled with forbearance and knowledge, his burden was heavy, and his renown is raised whenever he is mentioned.
DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.anchor: عن الحسن {ألم نشرح لك صدرك} قال: مليء حلما وعلما

DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.claim: He glosses the burden removed as the Prophet's sin and says it weighed heavily.
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {ووضعنا عنك وزرك} قال: ذنبك {الذي أنقض ظهرك} قال: أثقل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.claim: In the Hijaz dialect, وحده and forms such as ثلاثتهم are accusative; Banu Tamim instead match their case to the preceding noun.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.anchor: فيجرونه على الاسم الأول إن كان جرا فجرا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.claim: Al-Khalil says accusative ثلاثتهم means ‘only these, no others’; genitive forms generalize to everyone, like كلهم.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.anchor: الخليل رحمه الله أنه إذا نصب ثلاثتهم فكأنه يقول مررت بهؤلاء فقط لم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.claim: Al-Khalil explains accusative وحده and خمستهم by the verbal noun إفرادا, but Sībawayh calls this an analogy rather than an expression actually used in speech.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.anchor: نصب وحده وخمستهم أنه كقولك أفردتهم إفرادا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.claim: The Shammakh's poetic قضها بقضيضها is understood as انقضاضهم, a mass rush; Sībawayh uses it as an analogical explanation for accusative قضهم بقضيضهم.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.anchor: قول الشماخ # % أتنى سليم قضها بقضيضها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.claim: وحده derives from التفرد; خمستهم is accusative when meaning singling them out, but genitive when none are excluded, as with قضهم.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.anchor: الإفراد فى وحده والانقضاض فى قضهم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.claim: Some Arabs inflect قضهم like كلهم across the grammatical cases.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهوحدهومررتبهموحدهم.anchor: قضهم بمنزلة كلهم يجريه على الوجوه

NASHR:v1p219/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r1.claim: Ḍād is uniquely characterized by lengthening along its articulation and is difficult; pronounce it as ḍād rather than ẓāʾ, mixed dhāl, emphatic lām, or zāy.
NASHR:v1p219/r1.anchor: والضاد: انفرد بالاستطالة، وليس في الحروف ما يعسر على اللسان مثله.

NASHR:v1p219/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r2.claim: The popular saying that the Prophet was the most eloquent speaker of ḍād has no basis and is not sound.
NASHR:v1p219/r2.anchor: والحديث المشهور على الألسنة " أنا أفصح من نطق بالضاد " لا أصل له ولا يصح.

NASHR:v1p219/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r3.claim: Take special care to preserve ḍād beside ẓāʾ, emphatic letters, or similar sounds; أنقض ظهرك is an example beside ẓāʾ.
NASHR:v1p219/r3.anchor: فليحذر من قلبه إلى الظاء، لا سيما فيما يشتبه بلفظه نحو: ضل من تدعون، يشتبه بقوله: ظل وجهه مسودا،

NASHR:v1p219/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r4.claim: Ṭāʾ is the strongest emphatic letter; when a sākin ṭāʾ precedes tāʾ, assimilation must remain incomplete so its emphatic qualities survive.
NASHR:v1p219/r4.anchor: والطاء: أقوى الحروف تفخيما فلتوف حقها ولا سيما إذا كانت مشددة نحو: اطيرنا،

NASHR:v1p219/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r5.claim: The imams agree on making sākin ẓāʾ clear before tāʾ.
NASHR:v1p219/r5.anchor: والظاء: يتحفظ ببيانها إذا سكنت وأتى بعدها تاء نحو: أوعظت ولا ثاني له وإظهارها مما لا خلاف

NASHR:v1p219/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r6.speaker: ابن محيصن
NASHR:v1p219/r6.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin is reported to assimilate it while retaining its emphatic quality.
NASHR:v1p219/r6.anchor: نعم قرأنا بإدغامه عن ابن محيصن مع إبقاء صفة التفخيم.

NASHR:v1p219/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r7.claim: Avoid emphatic coloring of ʿayn; preserve its voicing and intensity before a voiceless letter, and make it clear before ghayn because the articulations are close.
NASHR:v1p219/r7.anchor: والعين: يحترز من تفخيمها، لا سيما إذا أتى بعدها ألف نحو: العالمين، وإذا سكنت

NASHR:v1p219/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p219/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p219/r8.claim: Make ghayn clear before every following letter, especially throat letters and in sukun; avoid moving it, particularly in لا تزغ قلوبنا, where it is close to qāf.
NASHR:v1p219/r8.anchor: والغين: يجب إظهارها عند كل حرف لاقاها، وذلك آكد في حرف الحلق وحالة الإسكان أوجب،

ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r1.speaker: أهل اللغة
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r1.claim: Lexicographers say a load anqaḍa a camel's back when strain makes it creak; naqīḍ al-mirjal is the pot's creak.
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r1.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة : أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة

ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r2.speaker: عباس بن مرداس
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r2.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse says the burden of caring for his people made his back creak.
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r2.anchor: قال عباس بن مرداس : وأنقض ظهري ما تطويت منهم

ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r3.speaker: جميل
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r3.claim: Jamīl's verse uses naqīḍ for the sound of ropes coming apart.
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r3.anchor: وقال جميل : وحتى تداعت بالنقيض حباله

ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:94:3/r4.claim: Naqīḍ denotes the sound of something breaking or coming loose.

ALUSI:94:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r1.claim: Anqada denotes a creaking or cracking sound; the usage extends beyond loads and men to joints, whose sounds make the back creak under a heavy burden.
ALUSI:94:3/r1.anchor: وهو صوت الانتقاض والانفكاك أعني الصرير ولا يختص بصوت المحامل والرجال بل يضاف إلى المفاصل

ALUSI:94:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r2.claim: Abbas ibn Mirdas uses anqada for a back creaking under strain from those for whom he felt concern, illustrating the word's bodily image.

ALUSI:94:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r3.claim: Attributing the creaking to the burden is a metaphorical attribution of an effect to its cause; the burden itself is the cause being carried.
ALUSI:94:3/r3.anchor: وإسناد الانقاض للحمل إسناد للسبب الحامل مجازاً

ALUSI:94:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r4.claim: One proposed burden is something the Prophet did before his mission that later weighed on him; its removal would mean forgiveness.
ALUSI:94:3/r4.anchor: ما صدر منه صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل البعثة مما يشق عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد

ALUSI:94:3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r5.claim: Another proposal is his lack of revealed knowledge of religious laws despite seeking them; removal means teaching him through revelation.
ALUSI:94:3/r5.anchor: أو غفلته عن الشرائع ونحوها مما لا يدرك إلا بالوحي

ALUSI:94:3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r6.claim: The burden may be his perplexity about matters such as fulfilling the mission or receiving revelation; its removal resolves that perplexity.
ALUSI:94:3/r6.anchor: أو حيرته عليه الصلاة والسلام في بعض الأمور كأداء حق الرسالة أو الوحي

ALUSI:94:3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r7.claim: The burden may be how extremely difficult the mission and revelation initially felt; removal is their easing through practice and habituation.
ALUSI:94:3/r7.anchor: فقد كان يثقل عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم في ابتداء أمره جداً

ALUSI:94:3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r8.claim: The burden may be seeing his people astray while unable to guide them because they would not obey or accept truth; its removal includes God guiding some, such as Hamza and Umar, to Islam.
ALUSI:94:3/r8.anchor: ما كان يرى صلى الله عليه وسلم من ضلال قومه مع العجز عن إرشادهم

ALUSI:94:3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r9.claim: The burden may be witnessing his people's transgressions in harming him; its removal is strengthening him to endure them.
ALUSI:94:3/r9.anchor: أو ما كان يرى من تعديهم في إيذائه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI:94:3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r10.claim: If the sūra came after Abu Talib and Khadija died, the burden may be grief for them; removal is consolation through ascension, angels' greeting, and beholding his greatest beloved and Lord.
ALUSI:94:3/r10.anchor: بناء على نزول الصورة بعد وفاتهما

ALUSI:94:3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r11.claim: Across these proposed meanings, the verse uses an extended illustrative metaphor, with placing the burden serving as a reinforcing extension of the image.
ALUSI:94:3/r11.anchor: ففي الكلام استعارة تمثيلية والوضع ترشيح لها

ALUSI:94:3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this wording does not establish the author's position on prophetic impeccability.
ALUSI:94:3/r12.anchor: وليس فيه دليل لنا في العصمة كما لا يخفى

ALUSI:94:3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:94:3/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan chooses to read placing the burden as figuratively expressing the Prophet's protection from sins and purification from impurities, hyperbolically denying such faults.
ALUSI:94:3/r13.anchor: واختار أبو حيان كون وضع الوزر كتابة عن عصمته

ALUSI:94:3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r14.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:94:3/r14.claim: Some say the burden is the community's, attributed to the Prophet because of his concern for it; its removal lifts worldly punishment while he remains among them and they seek forgiveness. Al-Ālūsī considers this remote.
ALUSI:94:3/r14.anchor: وقيل المراد وزر أمتك وإنما أضيف إليه

ALUSI:94:3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:3/r15.claim: The community-burden interpretation invokes the promise that God would not punish them while the Prophet was among them or while they sought forgiveness.
ALUSI:94:3/r15.anchor: ما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم

ALUSI:94:3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r16.speaker: أنس
ALUSI:94:3/r16.claim: Anas is reported to have read the phrase with the verbs حططنا and حللنا in place of وضعنا.
ALUSI:94:3/r16.anchor: وقرأ أنس وحططنا وحللنا مكان وضعنا

ALUSI:94:3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:3/r17.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI:94:3/r17.claim: Ibn Masud's variant reads وحللنا عنك وقرك in place of the standard wording.
ALUSI:94:3/r17.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وحللنا عنك وقرك

ALUSI:94:4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:4/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes the subtle sequence of raising remembrance after placing the burden, along with the conjunction and the added لك, discussed as before.
ALUSI:94:4/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى لطف ذكر الرفع بعد الوضع والكلام في العطف وزيادة لك كالذي سلف

BAGHAWI:94:3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:94:3/r1.claim: The burden weighed down and weakened his back until it made a cracking sound; naqīd means a sound.
BAGHAWI:94:3/r1.anchor: أثقل ظهرك فأوهنه حتى سمع له نقيض ، أي صوت

BAGHAWI:94:3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:3/r2.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI:94:3/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya and Abu ʿUbayda interpret it as God lightening the burdens of prophethood and carrying out its duties.
BAGHAWI:94:3/r2.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة : يعني خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها

BAYDAWI:94:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:3/r1.claim: The weight is compared to the creaking sound of a saddle under a heavy load.
BAYDAWI:94:3/r1.anchor: الذي حمله على النقيض وهو صوت الرحل عند الانتقاض من ثقل الحمل

BAYDAWI:94:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:3/r2.claim: The burden may have been the Prophet's lapses before his mission.
BAYDAWI:94:3/r2.anchor: وهو ما ثقل عليه من فرطاته قبل البعثة

BAYDAWI:94:3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:3/r3.claim: Another explanation is his lack of knowledge about rulings and religious laws.

BAYDAWI:94:3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:3/r5.claim: Another explanation is the weight of receiving revelation.
BAYDAWI:94:3/r5.anchor: أو تلقي الوحي ، أو ما كان يرى من ضلال قومه

BAYDAWI:94:3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:3/r6.claim: The burden may have been seeing his people's error while unable to guide them, or their persistence and excess in harming him when he called them to faith.
BAYDAWI:94:3/r6.anchor: أو ما كان يرى من ضلال قومه من العجز عن إرشادهم أو من إصرارهم وتعديهم في إيذائه حين دعاهم إلى الإيمان

BIQAI:94:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:3/r1.claim: Anqaḍa means making the back, the body's support, creak at the joints under a load, like a new saddle squeaking when tightly packed with heavy cargo.
BIQAI:94:3/r1.anchor: أي جعله وهو عماد بدنك تصوت مفاصله من الثقل كما يصوت الرحل الجديد إذا لز بالحمل الثقيل

BIQAI:94:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:3/r2.claim: The burden was the strain of being ordered to warn people who would resent criticism of their religion, ancestors, and judgment; the Prophet feared they would smash his head, and God eased him with signs, miracles, and protection.
BIQAI:94:3/r2.anchor: وذلك هو ما دهمه عندما أمر بإنذار قومه ومفاجأتهم بما يكرهون عن عيب دينهم وتضليل آبائهم وتسفيه حلومهم

BIQAI:94:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:3/r3.claim: The Prophet prayed that they would split his head and make it like a loaf; God then supported and protected him, as promised in 5:67.
BIQAI:94:3/r3.anchor: فقال :  "  يا رب إذن يثلغوا رأسي فيدعوه خبزة  "  فخفف سبحانه وتعالى عنه ذلك بما أظهر له من الكرامات

BIQAI:94:3/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:3/r4.claim: Biqāʿī says even the Prophet's family sometimes held him back from preaching, fearing the harm he might face, but he pulled away and delivered the message, including around the Night Journey.
BIQAI:94:3/r4.anchor: فصار أشفق أهله عليه يمنعه من بعض الإبلاغ ويمسك بثوبه لئلا يخرج إلى النار فيقول لهم ذلك

BIQAI:94:3/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI:94:3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Gabriel opened the Prophet's chest, removed a black clot from his heart and washed it away, then filled it with knowledge, faith, and wisdom; Biqāʿī says this enabled him to bear what others could not.
BIQAI:94:3/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هو أن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام شق صدره فأخرج منه قلبه فشرحه وأخرج منه علقة سوداء

BIQAI:94:3/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:3/r6.claim: Biqāʿī understands the burden literally as a weight, and legally as the consequence that would have followed from neglecting an obligatory command because it was onerous; God protected the Prophet from that.
BIQAI:94:3/r6.anchor: ولا شك أن ذلك وزر لغوي ،   وهو واضح ،   وشرعي بالمال على تقدير ترك الامتثال اللازم للاستثقال ،   وقد أعاذه الله من ذلك

BIQAI:94:3/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r7.speaker: الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:94:3/r7.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says sūras 93 and 94 together enumerate God's favors; they are separate because acquired blessings are listed first, lest they seem earned, followed by gifts begun before a person's existence.
BIQAI:94:3/r7.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : معنى هذه السورة من معنى السورة قبلها ،   وحاصل السورتين تعداد نعمه سبحانه وتعالى عليه

BIQAI:94:3/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:3/r8.speaker: الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:94:3/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr illustrates the sequence with God's address to Zechariah: after announcing John, God adds that He created Zechariah before, when he was nothing, a favor no one could claim to have earned.
BIQAI:94:3/r8.anchor: وتوهم استبداد الكسبية في وجود الولد غير خافية في حق من قصر نظره

DURR:94:2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the burden as the Prophet's sin and says the phrase about his back means it was heavy.
DURR:94:2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } قال : ذنبك { الذي أنقض ظهرك } قال : أثقل

DURR:94:3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the burden as the Prophet's sin and says the phrase about his back means it was heavy.
DURR:94:3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } قال : ذنبك { الذي أنقض ظهرك } قال : أثقل

IBNASHUR:94:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r1.claim: Anqada means to make something produce a naqīd, the creak of a saddle or load, joints, or cracking fingers; its base verb is intransitive and hamza makes it transitive.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r1.anchor: و { أنقض } جعل الشيءَ ذا نقيض ،  والنقيض صوت صرير المحمل والرحْل وصوتُ عظام المفاصل

IBNASHUR:94:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r2.claim: The burden is made the agent by figurative attribution, and the back is its object because hardship is pictured as a load; the compound image is of an overburdened carrier whose bones creak.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r2.anchor: وإسناد { أنقض } إلى الوِزر مجاز عقلي ،  وتعديته إلى الظهر تَبع لتشبيه المشقة بالحمل

IBNASHUR:94:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r3.claim: The elaborate image is a particularly fine compound comparison whose components can also be analyzed separately.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r3.anchor: وهو تمثيل بديع لأنه تشبيه مركب قابل لتفريق التشبيه على أجزائه

IBNASHUR:94:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r4.claim: Describing the burden this way completes the image by showing that it is immense.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r4.anchor: ووصف الوزر بهذا الوصف تكميل للتمثيل بأنه وزر عظيم

IBNASHUR:94:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r5.claim: The adjacent emphatic consonants ḍād and ẓā may make articulation heavy, but this does not reach the level of cacophony and is acceptable eloquent usage.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r5.anchor: واعلم أن في قوله :  { أنقض ظهرك } اتصالَ حرفي الضاد والظاء وهما متقاربا المخرج فربما يحصل من النطق بهما شيء من الثقل

IBNASHUR:94:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r6.claim: When syntax requires adjacent similar consonants, eloquent Arabs tolerate the slight heaviness; tajwid requires clearly distinguishing ḍād from ẓā, as here and in the cited examples.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r6.anchor: وقد أوصى علماء التجويد بإظهار الضاد مع الظاء إذا تلاقيا كما في هذه الآية وقوله :  { ويوم يعض الظالم }

IBNASHUR:94:3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:3/r7.claim: Imams carefully avoid substituting one letter for the other because jurists differ over when a poor reader's prayer is invalid, whether alone or leading a congregation.
IBNASHUR:94:3/r7.anchor: يتوخون الحذر من إبدال أحد هذين الحرفين بالآخر للخلاف الواقع بين الفقهاء في بطلان صلاة اللحَّان

IBNATIYYA:94:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r1.claim: One explanation says anqaḍa made the back thin and impaired under the weight.
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r1.anchor: و { أنقض } معناه جعله نقضاً ، أي هزيلاً معيباً من الثقل

IBNATIYYA:94:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r2.claim: Another explanation says it made a creaking sound; heavy loads cause what bears them to creak beneath them.
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه أسمع له نقيضاً وهو الصوت ، وهو مثل نقيض السفن وكل ما حملته ثقلاً فإنه ينتقض تحته

IBNATIYYA:94:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r3.speaker: عباس بن مرداس
IBNATIYYA:94:3/r3.claim: The cited line by ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās says a burden made his back creak or grow weak, illustrating the word.

IBNKATHIR:94:3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:94:3/r1.claim: Al-inqāḍ means a sound or creaking noise.

IBNKATHIR:94:3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:3/r2.speaker: غير واحد من السلف
IBNKATHIR:94:3/r2.claim: More than one early authority explains the burden as something that weighed heavily on the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR:94:3/r2.anchor: وقال غير واحد من السلف في قوله : { الَّذِي أَنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ } أي : أثقلك حمله .

MAWARDI:94:3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:3/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI:94:3/r1.claim: Anqada means made the back heavy; Ibn Zayd compares it to a camel weakened by a heavy load until it becomes naqḍ.
MAWARDI:94:3/r1.anchor: أي أثقل ظهرك ، قاله ابن زيد كما ينقض البعير من الحمل الثقيل حتى يصير نقضا

MAWARDI:94:3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:3/r2.claim: One view is that sins weighed down the Prophet until God forgave them.
MAWARDI:94:3/r2.anchor: أحدها : أثقل ظهره بالذنوب حتى غفرها

MAWARDI:94:3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:3/r3.claim: Another view is that the message weighed down the Prophet until he delivered it.
MAWARDI:94:3/r3.anchor: الثاني : أثقل ظهره بالرسالة حتى بلغها

MAWARDI:94:3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:3/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:3/r4.claim: A third view is that blessings weighed down the Prophet until he gave thanks for them.
MAWARDI:94:3/r4.anchor: الثالث : أثقل ظهره بالنعم حتى شكرها

NASAFI:94:3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:3/r1.claim: The burden weighed so heavily that it made a cracking sound.
NASAFI:94:3/r1.anchor: أثْقله حتى سمع نقيضه وهو صوت الانتقاض

QURTUBI:94:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r6.speaker: قتادة والحسن والضحاك
QURTUBI:94:2/r6.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the Prophet had sins weighing on him, which God forgave.
QURTUBI:94:2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة والحسن والضحاك : كانت للنبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ذنوب أثقلته ، فغفرها اللّه له

QURTUBI:94:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:2/r7.claim: The burden made his back so heavy that its creaking could be heard; Arabic usage also describes a load creaking on a camel and a saddle creaking.
QURTUBI:94:2/r7.anchor: أي أثقله حتى سمع نقيضه ، أي صوته . وأهل اللغة يقولون : أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة

QURTUBI:94:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:2/r8.claim: Jamīl's poem uses naqīḍ for the ropes' creaking and describes the front supports of the chest as nearly breaking.
QURTUBI:94:2/r8.anchor: قال جميل : وحتى تداعت بالنَّقِيضِ حبالُه

QURTUBI:94:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r9.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI:94:2/r9.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī says the burden would have weighed on him had God not pardoned him.
QURTUBI:94:2/r9.anchor: قال المحاسبي : يعني ثقل الوزر لو لم يعف اللّه عنه

QURTUBI:94:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r1.claim: The burden made the Prophet's back heavy and weakened it.
QURTUBI:94:3/r1.anchor: أي أثقله وأوهنه . قال : وإنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء

QURTUBI:94:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r2.claim: Prophets' sins are described as burdensome despite forgiveness because they are deeply concerned by them, regret them, and grieve over them.
QURTUBI:94:3/r2.anchor: وإنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء بهذا الثقل ، مع كونها مغفورة ، لشدة اهتمامهم بها

QURTUBI:94:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:94:3/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains removing the burden as lifting the Prophet's weight.
QURTUBI:94:3/r3.anchor: وقال السدي : " ووضعنا عنك وزرك " أي وحططنا عنك ثقلك

QURTUBI:94:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI:94:3/r4.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd says: We lifted your burden from you.
QURTUBI:94:3/r4.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود " وحططنا عنك وقرك

QURTUBI:94:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r5.claim: Some explain the burden as the weight of pre-Islamic sins.
QURTUBI:94:3/r5.anchor: وقيل : أي حططنا عنك ثقل آثام الجاهلية

QURTUBI:94:3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r6.speaker: الحسين بن المفضل
QURTUBI:94:3/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mufaḍḍal takes it to mean error and inadvertence.
QURTUBI:94:3/r6.anchor: قال الحسين بن المفضل : يعني الخطأ والسهو

QURTUBI:94:3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r7.claim: Some say the burden is the sins of the Prophet's community, attributed to him because his heart was occupied with them.
QURTUBI:94:3/r7.anchor: وقيل : ذنوب أمتك ، أضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بها

QURTUBI:94:3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r8.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI:94:3/r8.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā and Abū ʿUbayda say God lightened the burdens of prophethood and carrying it so it would not weigh on him.
QURTUBI:94:3/r8.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة : خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بها

QURTUBI:94:3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r9.claim: One account says revelation initially weighed on the Prophet until he nearly threw himself from a mountain; Gabriel showed himself and relieved his fear that his reason had changed.
QURTUBI:94:3/r9.anchor: وقيل : كان في الابتداء يثقل عليه الوحي ، حتى كاد يرمي نفسه من شاهق الجبل

QURTUBI:94:3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r10.claim: Another view says God protected him from bearing sin and kept him free of impurities through the forty years before revelation, which came to him purified.
QURTUBI:94:3/r10.anchor: وقيل : عصمناك عن احتمال الوزر ، وحفظناك قبل النبوة في الأربعين من الأدناس

RAZI:94:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r1.speaker: علماء اللغة
RAZI:94:3/r1.claim: Linguists explain that a back under a heavy load makes a faint naqīḍ sound, like loaded litters, ribs, or an overloaded camel; this pictures the burden on the Prophet.
RAZI:94:3/r1.anchor: قال علماء اللغة : الأصل فيه أن الظهر

RAZI:94:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r2.speaker: أصحاب جواز الصغائر
RAZI:94:3/r2.claim: Those who allow minor sins for prophets take the burden as a minor sin; its description as breaking the back reflects the Prophet's intense grief and remorse despite forgiveness.
RAZI:94:3/r2.anchor: الذين يجوزون الصغائر على الأنبياء عليهم السلام حملوا هذه الآية عليها

RAZI:94:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r3.claim: A second defense of the minor-sin reading is that the sin greatly affected the reward that would be lost through it, justifying the description of its weight.
RAZI:94:3/r3.anchor: وصفه بذلك لأن تأثيره فيما يزول به من الثواب عظيم

RAZI:94:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:94:3/r4.claim: Rāzī objects that the minor-sin defense conflicts with the Qāḍī's view that God must forgive minor sins: this verse presents forgiveness as a favor, which cannot be gratitude for an obligation.
RAZI:94:3/r4.anchor: أن العفو عن الصغيرة واجب على الله تعالى عند القاضي

RAZI:94:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r5.speaker: قتادة
RAZI:94:3/r5.claim: Qatāda says the burden was sins the Prophet had committed in the pre-prophetic Jāhiliyya, which weighed on him and were forgiven.
RAZI:94:3/r5.anchor: قال قتادة : كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب

RAZI:94:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r6.claim: Another non-sin reading is the heavy duties of prophethood: managing its charge and preserving its requirements and rights, which God made easy for him.
RAZI:94:3/r6.anchor: أن المراد منه تخفيف أعباء النبوة التي تثقل الظهر من القيام بأمرها

RAZI:94:3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r7.claim: The burden can mean distress at people changing Abraham's religion while the Prophet lacked power to stop them, until God strengthened him and commanded him to follow Abraham's way.
RAZI:94:3/r7.anchor: الوزر ما كان يكرهه من تغييرهم لسنة الخليل

RAZI:94:3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r8.claim: The burden may be the sins of the Prophet's community, which weighed on him as he wondered what he could do for them; God assured him He would not punish them while he was among them and promised intercession later.

RAZI:94:3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r9.claim: Another reading is that God protected the Prophet from a burden that would break his back if he had sinned; “setting down” is a metaphor for infallibility, illustrated by a report that God put him to sleep at a pre-prophetic wedding.
RAZI:94:3/r9.anchor: عصمناك عن الوزر الذي ينقض ظهرك

RAZI:94:3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r10.claim: In the illustrative report, the Prophet attended a wedding with drums and pipes before his mission, but God made him sleep until the next day's heat woke him.
RAZI:94:3/r10.anchor: ما روي أنه حضر وليمة فيها دف ومزامير قبل البعثة

RAZI:94:3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r11.claim: The burden may mean the awe and fear at the first meeting with Gabriel, when the Prophet trembled and nearly cast himself from a mountain, later becoming familiar and longing for Gabriel.
RAZI:94:3/r11.anchor: الوزر ما أصابه من الهيبة والفزع في أول ملاقاة جبريل

RAZI:94:3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r12.claim: The burden may be the abuse and insults that nearly broke the Prophet and made him tremble; God strengthened him until he could endure a bloodied face and pray for his people's guidance.
RAZI:94:3/r12.anchor: الوزر ما كان يلحقه من الأذى والشتم حتى كاد ينقض ظهره

RAZI:94:3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:94:3/r13.claim: In the account of enduring abuse, the Prophet said “God, guide my people,” when they had bloodied his face.
RAZI:94:3/r13.anchor: ثم قواه الله تعالى حتى صار بحيث كانوا يدمون وجهه

RAZI:94:3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r14.claim: If the sūra came after Abū Ṭālib and Khadīja died, the burden was grief at losing them; God lifted it by raising the Prophet to heaven, where angels greeted him and his renown was raised.
RAZI:94:3/r14.anchor: لئن كان نزول السورة بعد موت أبي طالب وخديجة

RAZI:94:3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:3/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:94:3/r15.claim: The burden may be the bewilderment before prophethood: the Prophet's reason made him feel overwhelmed by God's unrepayable blessings because he did not know how to serve God; revelation and duty taught him how to obey and relieved that shame.
RAZI:94:3/r15.anchor: أن المراد من الوزر والثقل الحيرة التي كانت له قبل البعثة

TAB:94:2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r5.speaker: author
TAB:94:2/r5.claim: Anqaḍa means that the burden made the back heavy and weakened it; Arabs describe an exhausted, emaciated camel as niqḍ safar, worn down by travel.
TAB:94:2/r5.anchor: الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ يقول :  الذي أثقل ظهرك فأوهنه ،   وهو من قولهم للبعير إذا كان رجيع سفر

TAB:94:2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:94:2/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses the burden as the Prophet's sin and says it weighed heavily on his back.
TAB:94:2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله :  وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  ذنبك .   وقوله :  أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ قال :  أثقل ظهرك

TAB:94:2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:2/r7.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had sins that weighed him down, which God forgave.
TAB:94:2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمَ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ :  كانت للنبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

ITQAN:v4p313/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p313/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p313/r1.claim: The argument for inimitability is that Quraysh's eloquent orators and poets never answered the challenge to produce a rival, although a short surah would have discredited the Prophet more effectively and cheaply than armed resistance; their failure over twenty-three years shows incapacity.
ITQAN:v4p313/r1.anchor: فدل ذلك العاقل على عجز القوم مع كثرة كلامهم وإستحالة لغتهم وسهولة ذلك عليهم وكثرة شعرائهم
